Underwhelming desk - concerns for longevity. Overall, this desk looks nice but leaves me concerned with its longevity due to flimsy feeling materials.  Pros: the desk looks nice, and is the advertised size. Height seems good, but I don’t yet have chairs to see how well it fits with a standard height chair. Relatively easy to assemble. Minimal screws and parts made it easier for me to assemble myself. The desk is also surprisingly light, and moves easily across the carpet for positioning. Metal Frame seems sturdy.  Cons: one of the tops came damaged, and shows just how thin the veneer on the top board is. The biggest con for me is how flimsy the whole top feels when any sort of weight is put on it. This seems to be largely due to the top support plank, which runs from one end to the other (also mdf). I believe it’s supposed to prop both of the desk top halves up to support the middle of the desk, but as you can see in the photo, this board was flexed and does not support both sides. Additionally, all screws were hand tightened, but you can see how the screw posts pulled into the soft mdf, immediately damaging. These will loosen up quickly over normal use of the desk and don’t leave me confident this desk will last very long with two people using it. Lastly, the description advertises cable management via the desk holes, but it also mentions built in usb ports, which are not on this desk. Misleading advertising.

Brand new microwave too powerful for this popper?. Excellent Design - Beautiful Piece - A Few Quality Control Issues. Over the last several years industrial style furniture and accents have become more and more popular - they are a wonderful trend combining the warm tones of wood with metal mesh and iron accents.  The juxtaposition makes the pieces interesting and unique.  This bar cabinet is a great example of industrial design combining black metal and iron with the cool grays of the wood.  It really is a beautiful and functional piece of furniture.  Assembly is not too difficult with instructions being on par for this type of product.  This is a great cabinet for holding wine glasses and bar accessories as well as displaying objects on the top.  The one issue I found during assembly relates to quality control.  As with most similar furniture products of this type it is constructed of laminated boards.  Several of the boards that make up the cabinet were separating from the outer laminate and a few of the corners had damage.  This is a combination of lack of quality control and inadequate packing materials for shipping.  I was able to repair some of these flaws but not all.  See photos.  While I wish I could give this product 5 stars, due to the issues mentioned above and the amount of repair work I had to preform prior to assembly, I must only give it 3 stars.

Memory Foam in Pieces Pillow; nice pillow; lovely pillowcases. I ordered the small square pillow. It comes with one extra pillowcase besides the one that is on the pillow. The pillowcases are quilted and relativelhy soft and thick. I do like the ear hole as it helps a little when resting on my left side. I particularly love this when resting the back of my head in the hole of the pillow. It is actually very comfortable.  The disappointment came when I opened the pillowcase. The entire pillow is composed of hundreds of memory foam pieces left over from the manufacturing process. It is contained via a thin mesh type cloth similar to what food store reusable shopping bags are made of. This means that if it rips, memory foam will be all over the interior pillowcase and the pillowcase cannot be changed. In addition, about 14 years ago I paid over $80 for two pillows that I thought were solid memory foam and wound up throwing them out after several weeks because the composition shifted making the pillows useless.  I am not saying this will happen with this pillow. However, be aware that this is NOT a solid memory foam pillow. It is made of memory foam pieces.  Despite this, I still like this pillow. Only time will tell if it will last. The current price of $38.89 is on the high side for this considering it is made of what I consider "memory foam waste."

OKAY BLENDER FOR THE PRICE; A COUPLE NICE FEATURES, ATTRACTIVE. The first thing I noticed about this blender is that the blending cup seemed very short and it seemed like it wouldn't hold as much as my other blender which hold 5 cups and is taller.  This holds 6 cups and the reason it can hold more without as much height is that the blending cup is bigger around.  The cup is nice thick glass and is one of the better features of the blender.  The blender is attractive, with a silver colored base, but the base doesn't appear to be metal, but more like a pastic coated with silver material.  Seems powerful enough to do most jobs, but probably more of a light duty blender.  The wattage is 550, which seemed like a lot, but in checking other blenders some are in the 700 to 750 watt range and I'm sure they go higher as well.  The gasket is not a separate piece which is a real plus.  I suppose 12 speeds is nice, but how many speeds do you really need?  I don't even use the 8 speeds on my old blender.  Instructions say that to blend hot liquids you need to leave the cover loose and cover it with a towel.  Seems like a hassle when other blenders will handle hot liquids without doing anything special.  When using it with hot food and liquids, you'll now have a dirty towel to wash.  I usually don't read what other reviewers say, as I don't want to be influenced one way or another, but I noticed several who had a problem with the plastic blender cup base breaking easily.  With a two year warranty and the low price of this blender, you probably can't go wrong, but it's not fun to wait for replacement parts.  You also have to search for your receipt and whatever else might be required for warranty service or return.  If I wanted a quality power tool, I wouldn't think twice about selecting Black & Decker as they make good power tools.  Are their small appliances as good?  Probably not.  I recommend buying a blender from a manufacturer who has a long history of making quality blenders.  Apparently Black & Decker acquired General Electric's small appliance division in 1984, so it would seem they have over 20 years of experience, but contrast this with the Waring Blender company that has been making blenders since the 1930's.  There are so many blenders available in the market and there probably isn't a lot of difference amongst them until you start getting up into higher prices.  Seems like there is a lot of competition in the market for blenders and this is a low end competitor is good enough for people who don't use a blender every day.  If you are constantly using your blender (like for a daily smoothie), select something more rugged that costs more.  This is by no means a food processor; I think it is wise to spend more and get a combo food processor and blender, which should serve your needs longer.  This is probably good for a cheap, attractive gift, especially for someone just starting out who really needs a blender.

Scary, Awkward-to-Use Grill Lacks On/Off Switch, Temperature Control. To only make grilled cheese sandwiches and panini, I thought this GEORGE FOREMAN 4-SERVING REMOVABLE PLATE GRILL AND PANINI PRESS (Black, GRP1060B) would be satisfactory for my needs.  Wrong, wrong, wrong!  My grill arrived new in the box, and it didn’t smoke or smell bad when I followed the manufacturer’s instructions to start by heating it empty for 15 minutes (to burn off any manufacturing oil or residue).  However, the budget-priced (about $29 on Amazon) grill is rather scary to use.  First, there is NO on/off switch or temperature control.  The grill heats when you plug it in, and it gets VERY hot in about 5 minutes.  You turn the grill off by unplugging it, and it takes quite a while to cool enough for you to remove the dishwasher-safe plates.  At least the cord doesn’t heat up, and it doesn’t spark when you unplug it.  Second, the hinge, which “adjusts” to handle thicker or thinner items placed on the grill, is very clunky.  When you open the lid and pull up, the hinge pulls up to make a wider space between the two grill plates. However, the hinge doesn’t pull evenly or all that easily.  Third, all of the black plastic parts (including the adjustable hinge) get hot when the grill is heated.  You really need to handle this grill with oven mitts or hot pads.  Fourth, the electrical cord is extremely short--shorter than most “short cord” countertop appliances that use a short cord as a safety feature.  Because the cord is so short, the cord won’t reach my kitchen countertop outlet unless I place the grill sideways on the countertop.  This makes it awkward to load the grill, which is really designed to be opened from the front.  The worst of these four bad features is the lack of a temperature control.  The only temperature is “very hot”, so it’s hard to toast grilled cheese sandwiches or panini sandwiches without burning them.  I wouldn’t dream of purchasing this grill for use in cooking meats or grilling vegetables.  While the grill isn’t exactly flimsy, it is clear that the manufacturer has put the minimum amount of material into the grill’s manufacture.  I’m pretty sure that the grill will burn out or quit working fairy soon if it is used at all regularly.

They Work but I Have my Concerns. Frozen pizzas are a popular food option in my house, thanks to our busy schedules and the desire to make food that is quick and requires little or no prep. We need something to help get the pizza out of the oven and cut/serve and this need convinced me to get the HOMEFAVOR Pizza Paddle Spatula.  Sold as a pair, the HOMEFAVOR Pizza Paddle Spatula is good for scooping a pizza from the oven and serving it on the table or counter. The boards have an extended handle and even have a slot so that you can hang them on a hook. The beveled edge helps make it easy to get the paddle underneath a pizza, lift, and remove from the oven. Once removed, the paddles double as a cutting board and serving plate.  I like these boards and have found them useful, but I do have concerns. For one, the moment they arrived, they already had small nicks in the edge of both paddles. The nick is too small to matter now, but given that these are made of wood and can so easily get a blemish like this, it makes me wonder how long until the same thing happens again and possible splinters start to show.  Another issue I have is with the size and thickness. The boards are a little thinner than I prefer and the size, well, it isn’t that big. It can handle only a small, store- bought pizza but that’s it. Anything larger will extend over the sides of the pan. However, besides pizza, you could also use these paddle pans for other things, like for serving meat and cheese. The handles make it easy to pick them up and transport from place to place with one hand.  We like to eat pizza and the HOMEFAVOR Pizza Paddle Spatula is a good addition to our kitchen. I am concerned about the nicks, the small size, and I am also a little concerned about excessive washing taking its toll. So, overall, this is a good item but it may not be adequate for some people.

Somehow deleting all sleep data caused the app to malfunction and close the moment it was started. I had to delete the app, reinstall and reregister everything. That took a few tries. Several days later the cable was accidentally unplugged from the adapter. I went through the setup procedure, nothing, several times. I read the help file and found out how to do a factory reset. I had to perform this seven times before the app would connect to the sensor again. I used the device for another week and suddenly it stopped collecting sleep data. For four days it sat under my mattress doing nothing. I tried contacting support and have not received a reply yet. An earlier question was answered fairly quick but I had to provide the serial number (adding a full day to the exchange) to get a simple data meaning question answered. On the fifth day the unit once again began sending data to the app. Is it defective? Perhaps. I'm unsure. But that leads me to my deepest concern. . . I don't trust the veracity of the data collected. It's supposed to be able to tell how long it takes you to fall asleep, when you're lightly or deeply asleep or in REM sleep as well as tracking when you snore, your pulse rate high, low and average through the night and how long it takes you to get up when you awake. I was impressed with all these bar graphs and data until I started looking closely. Every night I go to bed early due to pain and will spend up to a few hours reading or watching video on my tablet. when the bar graph said I was lightly asleep, I wasn't. When it said I was deeply asleep, I wasn't. I have no idea how, without seeing my eye movement, it can know I'm in REM sleep. I think one time it said I took a while to get to sleep but most nights while I lay there reading it was logging it as some form of sleep and my falling asleep taking only a few minutes. I know I snore, my scouts once dragged me out of the tent because I was so loud, so I guess the snoring detector is accurate. It  can also, some times, tell if you've taken a nap during the day and add that to the day's data though it appears there needs to be a susstantial time between getting up and going back for a nap otherwise the time gap gets logged as simply a really long interuption in your night's sleep. I tend to spend quite some time in bed on bad days and that seems to seriously confuse the device and app. It's a slick idea, nothing to wear, nothing to start or stop manually. Just stuff it under your mattress as directed and hey presto, sleep data. Too bad it's dreadfully inaccurate has connection issues and stops and starts recording data for no good reason. It would be great if it were even 80% accurate but I know for a fact it's no where near.

Decent Cutting Surface and Interesting Design, but Room for Improvement. I selected this cutting board set with the thought of using with with less countertop mess. It has not worked out quite like I envisioned. There are some design decisions that went into this product that merit a revisit.  This is a bamboo-surface cutting board with enough room to handle some of the larger jobs you might have in the kitchen - trimming a steak, cutting up butternut squash, breaking down a pineapple, and so on. I have no complaints with the size or the cutting surface which is smooth and not easily gashed without a serrated knife. Under the cutting surface are two steel catch bins with is great for prep work.  Where this product falls short is in two areas. First, it would have been useful to have a canal for draining off the juice trap. As received, the juice trap canal has no channel for drainage, so when it's full it just overflows. To drain it, it either needs to be inverted or the liquid needs to be mopped out. Second, this unit will not store compactly with the bamboo lids on the catch trays. Either the trays have to be removed for separate storage, or the tray lids stored upside down on top of the cutting board. Neither is ideal.  This is not a bad cutting board system, but there is room for improvement. The design is interesting and the craftmanship is fine, but minor oversights tarnish this enough from being a great product.

Simple Device for the Casual Wine Drinker. Oxo makes many handy gadgets that make life easier and the Oxo Steel Wine Aerator is a good one for those who drink wine. It makes the wine flow from the bottle in a widened stream, helping to aerate the wine, minimize spills, and make it taste better.  I don’t drink a large amount of wine, but I do drink some and I have found that aerators are nice for making wine pour more easily. This Oxo model is a little simpler than many others, but is also less expensive and gets the job done to a satisfactory level. I cannot tell a great difference in taste, but I certainly like the way the wine flows from the bottle. There is less chance of splashing and spilling when this device is attached to a bottle. I have found that wine pours out a little faster using this aerator than with others, and that makes me question its effectiveness. Still, it seems adequate for the job.  Oxo Steel Wine Aerator isn’t intended to be left inside the bottle, so don’t make that mistake. You still have to remove it and re- cork your wine for storage. I know that some people will go ahead and leave this in the bottle anyway, but it won’t protect wine like a cork will. Your wine won’t last long, so make sure you remove.  I own several Oxo products in my house and with the Oxo Steel Wine Aerator, we have another Oxo manufactured good to call our own. It isn’t an amazing aerator, so serious wine lovers might want to look elsewhere and invest a little more money in a more sophisticated product. But this is a good enough wine aerator to recommend. It basically does what it says and the price is right.

A Decent Looking Bed, A Few Disappointments. I really like the looks of this bed if you squint a little and look at it from a ways off. I have owned a couple of very nice wrought iron beds and really liked the looks but they were higher quality than this one.  I got a couple disappointments when I put it together.  The biggest of which is that my rigid box spring could not fit the bed lengthwise.  I ended up having to shift box springs around to get one that would fit the bed.  Set up was quick and easy.  I'm not sure why this is called a snap bed, or why the video advertisement says the pieces snap into place.  There is nothing that snaps, but it is an easy construction.  8 screws with the needed allen wrench included is nice.  The pieces fit together fine, and while this is not the sturdiest bed I've owned, it is as good as most inexpensive head and foot boards that attach to a bed frame.  The finish is a painted on fake brushed nickel.  There were two voids in the paint on mine and the threat that it can be scratched off.  The welds are large and rough, perhaps that was a look they were going for, but they are amateurish enough to look less elegant.  All in all, it's an OK bed, just not as good as I would have hoped from the photos and video.
